claims.text: The initial HfNbTaTiZr alloy is a random solid solution with substantial chemical disorder and local lattice distortion.
Monte Carlo simulation annealing or thermal treatment can induce chemical short-range order in a refractory high-entropy alloy.
The induced SRO preferentially forms HfTi and TiZr binary clusters.
The HfTi and TiZr clusters percolate into B2-like ordered domains.
The random and SRO states can be compared over 300–2000 K at identical bulk composition.
B2-like cluster regions locally regularize atomic positions.
The ordered cluster regions have less variation in atomic-size mismatch and force constants than the random environment.
Transition from the random state to ordered binary regions reduces the local RMS atomic displacement.
Mass and force-constant disorder in random alloys strongly scatters high-frequency phonons.
Reducing local lattice distortion suppresses high-frequency phonon scattering.
Percolation of low-distortion ordered regions creates preferential pathways for phonon transport.
Ordering shifts the high-frequency phonon DOS peak to higher frequency or energy.
Ordering increases phonon group velocity and mean free path.
The SRO/percolative state has higher lattice thermal conductivity than the random solid-solution state.
The conductivity increase occurs only after the SRO clusters form a connected network that reduces global lattice-distortion variance.
Isolated, non-percolating SRO clusters do not produce the proposed conductivity increase.
Phase-separated precipitates with substantial interfacial strain decrease conductivity through interface scattering.
Prior evidence shows that SRO can affect dislocation mobility and add strengthening in a refractory high-entropy alloy.
The proposed DOS shift and the percolation threshold in HfNbTaTiZr have not been empirically established by the cited evidence.
A lower high-frequency DOS peak, higher atomic-displacement amplitude, or decreased lattice conductivity in a verified percolative ordered state would falsify the proposed mechanism.
